slides.kicker: CONSUMER FINANCE / CONVENIENCE VS. CORPORATE FLOAT
slides.headline: Your Rewards. Their Interest-Free Financing.
slides.subheadline: Follow prepaid dollars into financing benefits and nonredemption revenue.
slides.standfirst: The pitch: **easier payments and more rewarding purchases**.
slides.svgBlueprint: viewBox='0 0 952 650'. Establish shared tokens: --accent:#FF4D00; --paper:#0D0E12; --surface:#161820; --ink:#F1F3F9; --border:#262938. Construct an original closed-loop gift-card specimen at x=52,y=80,w=350,h=220, rotated -12 degrees around its center. Connect its lower edge through a flanged orange inlet to a cylindrical corporate cash tank centered at x=637,y=325. Tank bounds are x=447–827,y=110–538, with elliptical ends, visible internal fluid, a lower purchase outlet and a separate accounting-recognition branch. The liquid is conceptual, not a measured liability balance or segregated cardholder reserve. Anchor short SVG callouts 'PREPAY', 'PURCHASE' and 'BREAKAGE' to their respective connectors; body explanation remains HTML. Do not depict an EMV chip or contactless capability as a factual feature of the Starbucks gift card. All dark surfaces require visible outlines: structural strokes use var(--ink) at 0.25 opacity and 1.5–2px width; accent pathways use 3px strokes; registration marks use 0.4 opacity. The breakage branch ends at a revenue-register dial rather than a cash outlet, distinguishing accounting recognition from physical cash movement.

slides.headline: Convenience Keeps You Coming Back
slides.subheadline: The customer promise doubles as a business strategy.

items.title: THE PROMISE
items.body: Starbucks markets **easier shopping and rewarding payments**.

items.title: THE OBJECTIVE
items.body: Starbucks explicitly targets **more frequent store visits**.

slides.svgBlueprint: viewBox='0 0 952 420'. Create one continuous checkout-and-return mechanism, not two floating icons. At x=65–335,y=80–340, a physical gift card enters a countertop reader with an angled face, card slot, display bezel and tactile keys. The reader connects to an arcing return rail that wraps around a recognizable café entrance at x=585–865,y=70–345. One orange outbound arrow represents the payment interaction; three ink return arrows describe repeated visits without suggesting a measured frequency. Place anchored labels 'PAYMENT' and 'RETURN VISIT' alongside the rail. The storefront has a door, handle, transom, threshold and striped awning, avoiding an empty rectangular building. Keep all explanatory copy in HTML. Use outlined var(--surface) shells, var(--ink) structural strokes at 0.25 opacity, 3px orange focal paths and registration marks at 0.4 opacity. Connect the two bottom editorial sections back to the reader and return rail with terminating leader dots.

slides.headline: That Liability Is Not Cash

items.title: BALANCE MIX
items.body: The liability includes **loyalty rewards**, not cards alone.

items.title: FLOW MIX
items.body: Deferrals include **Stars earned**, not just cash loads.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use two coordinated half-width SVG artboards, each viewBox='0 0 448 420'. Left artboard: construct a bound accounting ledger at x=38–410,y=36–330. A gift-card specimen enters one side; a star-shaped loyalty token enters the other. Both terminate at a single ledger binding, establishing that the reported liability combines cards and rewards. Mount '$1,751.7' on an integrated ledger total plate at x=224,y=370; the exact unit, label and date belong in the associated HTML caption. Right artboard: build a mechanical intake register at x=35–413,y=46–328, with one physical card-load inlet and one distinct Stars-earned inlet. Their traces converge on the register, not on a cash reservoir. Anchor '$15,245.8' below its counter housing. Do not assign proportions to either component, because component shares are not supplied. The paired instruments share one visual baseline but no equal-sign connector. Use real short SVG labels 'CARDS', 'REWARDS', 'LOADS' and 'STARS'; never represent ledger text with hatch marks. Structural strokes are 1.5–2px ink at 0.25 opacity; accent convergence traces are 3px.

slides.headline: Cash Arrives Before The Coffee

items.title: PAY FIRST
items.body: Your **prepayment fills Starbucks’ cash tank** before fulfillment.

items.title: BUY LATER
items.body: Purchases **draw down balances**; cards never expire.

items.title: RECOGNIZE BREAKAGE
items.body: Expected nonredemption **becomes revenue proportionately with redemptions**.

slides.svgBlueprint: viewBox='0 0 952 420'. Place a continuous vertical process spine at x=92,y=32–388, with milestone nodes at y=74,210,346. A compact gift card at x=160,y=38 feeds a cylindrical tank bounded by x=390–650,y=48–337. The top inlet is orange and clearly enters before the purchase outlet. At y=245, the purchase branch runs to a cup at x=790,y=230; pair it with a narrow account-balance gauge showing drawdown without a numerical scale. At y=346, a dashed accounting branch links the redemption mechanism to a revenue-register wheel at x=784,y=345. This is not a literal cash drain: it encodes expected nonredemption recognized proportionately with redemptions. Show the retained prepaid-use zone with an outlined bracket, not an assertion that the entire tank is unredeemed card cash. Short anchored labels are '01', '02', '03', 'CASH IN', 'REDEEM' and 'RECOGNIZE'. Preserve clear separation between solid cash-flow piping, account-balance movement and dashed recognition linkage. All explanatory text belongs in the three HTML milestone rows below.

slides.headline: Revenue Is Not Reported Profit

telemetry.label: million · calculated breakage revenue from expected nonredemption

items.title: COMPANY OPERATED
items.body: Company-operated stores recognized **$200.4 million** breakage revenue.

items.title: LICENSED STORES
items.body: Licensed stores recognized **$22.0 million** breakage revenue.

slides.footer: Disclosed components added—not separately reported profit.
slides.svgBlueprint: viewBox='0 0 952 420'. Build a wide thermal accounting receipt occupying x=70–882,y=24–396. Its silhouette has curled upper corners, a lightly tinted paper surface, visible perimeter and a serrated lower cut. Two attached source-entry tabs identify the inputs through HTML captions beneath the artwork; inside the receipt, place the arithmetic as genuine SVG text: '$200.4' at x=150,y=112, '+' at x=407,y=112 and '$22.0' at x=498,y=112. Place the anchored unit 'million' beside the input row. A ruled subtotal line leads to the dominant '$222.4' centered at x=476,y=258, with the anchored unit 'million' below. A precision bracket and registration marks make the total feel measured, not promotional. Add a real variable-width barcode in the lower-left receipt margin and a small 'FY2025' plate in the lower-right. Barcode is decorative, not a purported source-document identifier. This specimen represents calculated revenue arithmetic, not an actual Starbucks receipt or a separately reported profit measure. Structural lines use ink at 0.25 opacity; reserve orange for the plus sign, total underline and one verification mark.

slides.headline: Reloads Keep Their Tank Filled
slides.subheadline: Starbucks receives financing before fulfilling your prepaid purchases.

items.title: COMPLETED LOADS
items.body: This cancellation provision **cannot reverse completed loads**.

slides.footer: Legal and contractual refund exceptions remain.
slides.svgBlueprint: viewBox='0 0 952 420'. Build a horizontal authorization rail at y=228 from x=58 to x=895. A scheduled-reload clock assembly sits at x=180,y=145; an adjustable cancellation gate crosses the rail at x=400; a completed-load ratchet sits at x=638; the rail then feeds a small cylindrical cash tank at x=790–910,y=145–345. Mark the scheduled reload as T at x=638 and the deadline as T − 24 h at x=400, with an anchored dimension bracket between them. Use an open gate and a return branch before the deadline. Beyond the completed-load ratchet, show a solid forward path and a small blocked reverse arrow tied specifically to this cancellation provision—not a universal prohibition on refunds or legal remedies. The tank is schematic, with no invented monetary scale. Render 'T − 24 h', 'T' and 'COMPLETED' as short anchored SVG labels; the exact contractual wording belongs in HTML. Use 3px orange for the release rail and deadline pointer, 1.5–2px ink structure at 0.25 opacity, and clearly outlined surface fills.

slides.headline: Real Financing. Not An Unregulated Bank.
slides.subheadline: No interest. No FDIC insurance. Consumer-protection laws still apply.

items.title: REFUND LIMITS
items.body: Generally nonrefundable; **legal and contractual exceptions apply**.

items.title: EGIFT EXCEPTION
items.body: Unused eGifts: **refunds require the original receipt**.

slides.footer: Prepayment buys future purchases—not an interest-bearing deposit.
slides.svgBlueprint: Use two coordinated half-width SVG artboards, each viewBox='0 0 448 420'. Left artboard: a gift card at x=28,y=40 feeds a cutaway corporate reservoir bounded by x=157–384,y=82–340. Add a small financing-time dial, purchase outlet and retained-use bracket. Do not depict a bank charter, insured vault, FDIC seal or segregated reserve. Anchor short callouts 'NO INTEREST' and 'NO FDIC INSURANCE' to the card account, not to an institution-wide insurance assertion. Right artboard: construct a consumer-rights docket with layered sheets at x=42–300,y=36–350. An unused eGift voucher and original-receipt specimen meet at a hinged review gate at x=305,y=235. An open return arrow leaves the gate to show that exceptions exist, without depicting approval as automatic. The receipt has a serrated edge, variable-width barcode and a real short SVG label 'RECEIPT'. Add a small outlined 'UNUSED' status tab to the eGift specimen. All legal explanations remain HTML. Use visible 1.5–2px ink outlines at 0.25 opacity; orange highlights the financing inlet and the exception-review path, giving the two ideas equal visual legitimacy.
